lines.en: I tap on Tsubasa’s name in my phone with a bit more optimism than normal- but it’s not because I understand her any better now.
And it’s also not because I foresee any sort of progression in regard to our (but mostly her) super secret plan to relocate a gyaru.
That still hinges upon me to some extent and, with no further movement from Chika on top of my customary lack of action, things will likely stay the same for at least a little while longer.
But as these last few sentences have pulled me from the beaten path we were walking together just moments ago, I’d like to now confess why I’ve been stricken with optimism.
You see, last night, I had another dream — and in it, the paint peeled from off of the walls in my home, but it was only the first layer.
The layer beneath told me a secret.
It said “The past will catch up to me” before that layer peeled off as well.
Then suddenly, my house was gone and I was all alone in a field full of sunflowers.
I plucked one from the ground and pressed it to my tongue.
And I remembered why I’ve always loved them.
: Ahh, Arakawa-Sensei. Excellent timing. I was just about to call you.
: Really? You never call me.
: Well, today is a special exception as you are being cordially invited to join me in my office for a bit of a meeting.
: Does this involve Chika again? Because I still haven’t-
: It does not. This is a matter regarding my family and yours.
: If this is a joint marriage proposal, I’d like to remind you I have basically nothing to offer.
: Why, that’s not true at all. But you can take solace in the fact that it’s something completely different.
: Can...you tell me what that something is?
: I will! But I would like you to actually be here first.
: I guess I’ll...start walking then.
: Oh, that won’t be necessary. Someone should-
: Arakawa-sama, please get into the vehicle.
: What the fuck? Where did you come from?
: Oh, splendid! It sounds as if your car has already arrived!
: You’ll be escorted directly to me upon arrival. I’m looking forward to it.
: Arakawa-sama, the mistress is waiting. Please get into the vehicle.
: Fine, okay. But I’m not wearing another blindfold.
I get into the back of the car and am quickly whisked off to Tsukioka Manor for an impromptu meeting with someone I am now tempted to refer to as “the mistress.”
The main problem here is that I’d likely be unable to say this without a sarcastic undertone that would make it sound as if I’m mocking her. And I would prefer not being assassinated today.
As such, I will respect Tsubasa as much as I possibly can.
And I will only try to have sex with her if I think she really wants it.
Anything else is just too risky.
: Welcome to yet another brand new room — and a rare one at that. You join the ranks of the lucky few who have been able to sit with me at this table. It’s something you should be very proud of.
: And all I had to do to get here was make your daughter want to bone me.
: My bad. I’m not very good at formal meetings like this.
: It’s fine. It’s not as if anyone is listening in on us. I just can’t help but be taken aback by your...casual brazenness.
: No one’s ever had the courage to say such a thing to my face before.
: But that’s just one more thing that makes you all the more interesting.
: Am I allowed to flirt back or does that go against manor policy?
: Go ahead. This isn’t me accepting your advances, but I’m curious to see what you’d say.
: Uhh...
: Nothing? Are you not attracted to me after all?
: It’s just...kind of hard when you’re directly challenging me.
: Then let’s just say you said something flattering and that I laughed. And that we left it at that before moving onto other things.
: Ahh, so it’s not just a meeting where you flirt with me. I was beginning to think the arranged marriage was for us.
: Oh, look! You managed to flirt after all. That was actually rather cute. Good job, Sensei.
: And now it’s weird again since you’re complimenting me.
: Does this feel awkward for you? Would we have been better off in the garden?
: I know it might seem as if I’m trying to put myself in a position of power here, but the truth is I just had a lot of work to get done and all of that work is in here.
: It does...but it would feel less awkward if you’d just tell me why I’m here already.
: Then, to save both of us the discomfort, I’ll get right to it.
: When we last left off on the stairs of your school’s archery range, you made it apparent that you weren’t interested in divulging any of your...personal details to me.
: To which I responded that I would look into them on my own.
: And...I’m assuming this meeting is in response to you doing just that.
: And in that assumption, you would be correct...Akira.
Welp, make it four people who now know that name.
: Is it okay if I call you that? It seems only fair, what with me just being “Tsubasa” to you and all.
: Is “the mistress” preferable? Because that’s how the driver earlier referred to you and I was thinking it might be fun to try that.
: If you’re planning on working for me instead of with me, such a title would be fine. But I’d prefer to keep things a bit more amiable between us.
: So...what do you want?
: Why do you think I want something?
: The look into my background...the raised eyebrow...the way your hands are folded together...all signs point to you wanting something.
: What did you find out? Why did it warrant calling me to your home?
: What I found out is that you’re a much more...legitimate teacher than you present yourself to be.
: Your grades in school were exceptional...among the top of your class even. And every single career assessment survey you ever filled out all had the same exact aspiration listed on them. Teacher.
: You read my...career assessment surveys?
: If it’s something you’ve written on paper and handed over to someone, chances are I have access to it.
: You were quite the poet as well. Do you still write?
: Ara- Ahem...Akira-san?
: No. I don’t write anymore.
: Did something happen?
: Is that a troubling question?
: I don’t want to talk about it.
: So much for not being very interesting.
: Is that all, mistress?
: Oh my. I didn’t mean to anger you. I was simply curious about how you became the way you are today.
: No amount of records or poetry can properly retell the story of the life you’ve lived. So I was hoping you would share a piece or two of that with me.
: And I was hoping my private life would stay a little more, you know, private.
: In my defense, you didn’t try to stop me when I explicitly told you this was coming. I’d not have pried if I’d only known you were against it.
: It’s...fine.
: To be honest, the past is a bit of a touchy subject for me as there’s still a lot of it I don’t remember.
: That you don’t...remember?
: Just call it amnesia. That’s the simplest way to explain it.
: Your medical records mention nothing about amnesia. Could I be missing documents? I’m normally so good at this.
: It’s not something that would be documented. And yeah, there was a thing that happened.
: But I’m nowhere even close to being able to talk about it with anyone yet...let alone someone who’s only probing me to satisfy her own curiosity.
: You say that as if I don’t care about you. That hurts.
: Do you, though?
: Of course.
: But it’s only because of the role I play in your scheme, right? It’s only because Touka needs me in order to...move forward and adhere to the plan you have for her or whatever.
: Am I wrong?
: Hah...
: I sincerely apologize, Akira-san.
: I must have let my guard down at the archery range as it’s very clear now that I didn’t properly think my words through.
: If I had, you wouldn’t think this way at all.
: It’s true that I fancy pulling the strings...and that there is nothing more important to me than ensuring my daughters’ futures play out just as smoothly as mine.
: But that doesn’t mean I see you as nothing more than a hunk of meat...ready to be thrown on the grill so they can go to sleep sated and satisfied.
: I see you as an equal.
: You don’t see anyone as an equal.
: That is simply not true. And if I’ve come across that way, it means I must have improperly conveyed other words of mine as well.
: Consistent poor-wording aside...what does that have to do with our families? What was so important that you went out of your way to borderline kidnap me?
: I would like to ask you for a favor.
: Big surprise. Who do you want me to reel in now?
: My daughter.
: Touka’s too perceptive to-
: My other daughter.
: ...What?
: Tsukasa-darling! Could you come in here?
: Yes, Mother?
: Tsukasa, how are you faring in your studies?
: Exceptionally, Mother. There are no problems at all.
: But are you enjoying yourself?
: Yes, Mother.
: It’s okay to be honest right now, dear. This isn’t a formal meeting.
: But-
: Oh. It’s just Jeeves. What is he doing here?
: Tsukasa, how would you feel about Arakawa-sensei taking over your lessons?
: Really?! Can he?! That’s okay?!
: Uhh...
: Is there a problem, Arakawa-sensei? It’s not as if you don’t already have experience tutoring girls her age, correct?
: Tsukasa is on another level. I can’t keep up with whatever she’s being taught right now.
: The same goes for Touka and she’s been exceptional under your guidance. I assume you’ll have no trouble replicating that same success with someone younger.
: Don’t worry, Jeeves! If I’m too smart for you to tutor, I’ll just teach you instead! It’ll be fun!
: I don’t have the time to come here every day, Tsubasa. I’m already teaching at school and there’s no way they’d admit Tsukasa at her age.
: The school will do whatever I tell them to. But that’s not what I had in mind.
: Then what-
: I was planning on having my daughters move into your new building as well.
: What?
: Is something wrong, dear?
: I’m...going to live with Onee-sama?
: There are some preparations that still need to be made. But that is the plan as of right now, yes.
: And...what...what did Onee-sama say?
: That she’ll uphold her duty as the heir to the foundation and do exactly as I ask. Just as I expect you to do as well.
: But...that means I’ll spend even less time with you and Papa than I do now! And I barely ever get to spend time with you in the first place!
: What are you saying, dear? You’re with me almost every waking hour of the day.
: That’s not what I mean! You’re always working and Papa never wants to see me and I’m tired of you always trying to get rid of me! I didn’t do anything wrong!
: Tsukasa?...
: I want to stay here with you! I don’t want to leave yet!
: Tsu-
: I’m going to my room!
: Tsukasa! Wait!
: You know, if I knew that’s what you were ramping up to, I probably could have prevented this.
: What? How? I don’t even understand what just happened.
: She’s lonely. I’ve known that since National Tsukasa Day.
: How is she lonely? She’s surrounded by either attendants or me for nearly twenty-four hours every day. She gets everything she wants and does everything she wants. How is that lonely?
: All of that might be true, but when was the last time the two of you did something fun together? Where you weren’t just being dragged along as a babysitter.
: I’m not...
: It’s the same with Touka too, but to a much lesser extent since you still make time to drop by her dorm room every now and then.
: Plus she’s also mature enough to shelve those feelings and hide them from you. Tsukasa can’t do that.
: Hah...
: You’re right...
: You’re absolutely right.
: I don’t know how I didn’t realize that earlier.
: Just...too busy focusing on other things, I guess.
: All other things are now on hold — and that includes this meeting. It’s clear that I need to have a talk with both of my daughters.
: Does that mean I can stop teaching Touka things? She keeps trying to learn while she’s in school and I’m not sure how to handle it.
: You’ll continue on with Touka exactly as you’ve done thus far. And Tsukasa will follow shortly after things are remedied between the two of us.
: Why do you even want me to teach her? I don’t get it.
: You don’t need to.
Tsubasa stands up from her desk, prompting me to do the same as I’m sure I’ll be escorted out of the manor momentarily.
I get that her methods in growing her daughters can be a little...unorthodox, but sending a girl Tsukasa’s age to live in the same building as me is something I didn’t even think she’d consider.
I mean...why would she? Chika makes sense. Touka kind of makes sense...But what could Tsukasa gain from that?
Is it the risk that would help her grow?
Have I fallen so far that there’s any risk at all?
I just don’t understand.
: That look on your face tells me I should clarify something.
: Why were you...sending her to live with me?
: It was just the same building. It’s not as if I was asking her to sleep in your bed.
: Besides, when I was her age, I had an apartment as well. I just never had any use for it.
: And she does?
: I thought so. But that was before the screaming and the revelation of her loneliness. Now, I know I was wrong. That happens sometimes, you know.
: Just because I’m powerful doesn’t mean I don’t make mistakes. I’m as flawed and vulnerable as everyone else.
: I’m the same as you.
: That’s what I meant by equal.
: And, Akira-sensei...
: I’m not trying to insinuate anything here...but my decision to send her to Touka’s new apartment complex was not for the reasons you may think.
: And...what do you assume I thought?
: Let’s just say that there are different stages of development my daughters need to go through before I will fully acknowledge them as women.
: Touka is in the final phase of development...and I trust that she’s mature enough to make decisions in regard to how and when she uses her body.
: You could lay as many fingers as you want on her and I’d think nothing of it.
: But if you believe for even a moment that I’d apply that same ideology to Tsukasa...we’d have a bit of a problem on our hands.
: I would like to avoid that. Wouldn’t you?
: Definitely. I wouldn’t have even thought about that.
: Are you telling me you don’t find Tsukasa pretty?
: That...
: Just a joke to lighten the mood. There was no right answer there.
: Plus, once Chika moves in, I doubt you’ll have time to even think of doing such things with other girls.
: But in the event that both she and my oldest daughter can not satisfy your...urges...
: All you need to do is let me know and...arrangements can be made.
: That...was a joke too, right?
: I wonder.
I exit the manor both terrified and aroused.
And after spending a lot more time with her recently, I think that’s...just the sort of effect Tsubasa is going to have on me.
I understand her, but I don’t.
I’m afraid of her, but I’m not.
I can’t explain it.
But there is one thing I know for sure.
And it’s that I need to keep her close.
Because I know that if I don’t, I’ll be peering over my shoulder for the rest of my life.
: What the fuck are arrangements?
Tsubasa’s affection has increased to [tsubasa_love]!
